lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 17: scheduling basics
lesson.description: Steer Pods onto the right nodes with nodeSelector and node affinity, keep replicas apart or together, and spread them evenly across zones.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a four-node kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Label your nodes, then say where Pods must or should go. Use topology spread to survive a zone loss, and read FailedScheduling events when a Pod waits.

boards.title: Four ways to place a Pod

rows.name: nodeSelector
rows.role: Every listed label must match. No operators.

rows.name: Node affinity
rows.role: Required rules use In, NotIn and Exists. Preferred rules add a weight from 1 to 100.

rows.name: Pod affinity
rows.role: Place this Pod near, or away from, Pods with a label, per node or per zone.

rows.name: Spread
rows.role: Keep the count of matching Pods within maxSkew across a topology key.

rows.name: gpu=true
rows.role: needs-gpu stayed Pending until a node was labeled gpu=true. No reapply.

rows.name: Preferred SSD
rows.role: Required zones a and b, preferred disktype=ssd at weight 80. All 4 replicas landed on worker2.

rows.name: Anti-affinity
rows.role: Required on kubernetes.io/hostname. Three replicas, one per worker. The fourth stayed Pending.

rows.name: maxSkew 1
rows.role: Six shop replicas sat 2/2/2. With worker3 cordoned, nine replicas sat 3/3/2 and one stayed Pending.

items.what: The scheduler filters out nodes where a Pod cannot run, scores the rest, and binds the Pod to the top-ranked one.
Required pod affinity on the zone key placed the workers on the same node as cache, worker2.
After uncordon, the nine shop replicas settled at 3/3/3.
Read FailedScheduling. The cordoned spread case said 2 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints.

commands.note: one Pod per node when required

homework.intro: Use a kind cluster with several worker nodes and the namespace k8s-from-zero. The lesson's nodes are k8s-ep16-worker, worker2 and worker3. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What does the scheduler do with the nodes that remain after filtering?
exercises.a: It scores them and binds the Pod to the top-ranked node. Filtering removes nodes where the Pod cannot run.

exercises.q: How is required node affinity different from nodeSelector?
exercises.a: nodeSelector requires every listed label to match, with no operators. Required node affinity adds operators such as In, NotIn and Exists. Preferred affinity adds a weight from 1 to 100 and still schedules when the preferred nodes are full.

exercises.q: What does whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule do to a topology spread constraint?
exercises.a: The Pod stays Pending rather than breaking maxSkew. ScheduleAnyway still places it and scores the imbalance.

exercises.q: Apply pod-gpu.yaml before any node has gpu=true. What happens, and what changes after you label one node?
exercises.a: needs-gpu stays Pending with a FailedScheduling event. After kubectl label node k8s-ep16-worker3 gpu=true it schedules, without applying the Pod again.

exercises.q: Scale the required hostname anti-affinity Deployment to 4 on three workers. Where does the fourth Pod sit?
exercises.a: It stays Pending. Required anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname cannot place two of those Pods on one node, and only three workers qualify.

exercises.q: With spread maxSkew 1 and worker3 cordoned, scale shop to 9. What counts did the lesson record?
exercises.a: 3 on zone-a, 3 on zone-b, 2 on zone-c, and one Pod Pending because 4 against 2 would be a skew of 2. The event said 2 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: A Pod stays Pending. What does the lesson tell you to read?
exercises.a: kubectl describe pod NAME, the FailedScheduling event. A node affinity or selector miss, an anti-affinity miss, and Insufficient cpu are different reasons.

exercises.q: Required pod anti-affinity on hostname, and you want four replicas. What limit does the lesson name?
exercises.a: The replica count cannot exceed the number of nodes that match. Three workers means the fourth Pod waits.

exercises.q: You prefer SSD nodes but the app must still run when they are full. Which rule does the lesson use?
exercises.a: Preferred node affinity with a modest weight. Required affinity would leave the Pod Pending instead.
